'''Helga Ernestine Rafelski,''' (née Betz) (3 September 1949 – 5 November 2000<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rafelski|first=Johann|year=2020|title=Discovery of Quark-Gluon Plasma: Strangeness Diaries|journal=The European Physical Journal Special Topics|language=en|volume=229|issue=1|pages=1–140|doi=10.1140/epjst/e2019-900263-x|arxiv=1911.00831|bibcode=2020EPJST.229....1R|s2cid=207869782 |issn=1951-6355}}</ref>) was a German [[Particle physics|particle physicist]]. She got her professional degree from [[Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rafelski|first1=H.|last2=Fink|first2=B.|year=1974|title=Particle Number Dependence of Collective Properties of Nuclei in the Rare Earth Region|journal=Zeitschrift für Naturforschung A|volume=29|issue=8|pages=1131–1137|doi=10.1515/zna-1974-0804|bibcode=1974ZNatA..29.1131R|s2cid=3476447 |issn=1865-7109|doi-access=free}}</ref> her master's degree from [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] in 1977 and her [[PhD]] from [[University of Cape Town]] in 1988 under the advisement of Raoul D. Viollier.<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Rafelski|first=Helga E.|year=1988|type=PhD|title=Muon regeneration in muon catalyzed dt-fusion|url=https://open.uct.ac.za/handle/11427/16012|publisher=University of Cape Town —UCT-TP-100-88|oclc=890420063|place=Cape Town}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Author profile for Helga E. Rafelski|url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1021604|website=Inspire HEP|access-date=2020-05-12}}</ref> She studied [[Muon-catalyzed fusion|muon-catalysed fusion]] and [[relativistic heavy-ion collisions]].

Returning from [[South Africa]], Rafelski held a visiting position at [[Goethe-Universität Frankfurt am Main]] where she worked with [[Berndt Müller]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rafelski|first1=H.E.|last2=Müller|first2=B.|year=1990|title=PC-fortran programs for muon reactivation calculations in muon-cataluzed fusion|journal=Computer Physics Communications|language=en|volume=59|issue=3|pages=521–526|doi=10.1016/0010-4655(90)90093-G|bibcode=1990CoPhC..59..521R}}</ref> In-between other appointments she was a scientific associate at [[CERN]] in the Data Handling Division.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Hagedorn|first1=Rolf|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/132931|title=SIGMA, a new language for interactive array-oriented computing (CERN-78-12)|last2=Reinfelds|first2=Juris|last3=Van Hove|first3=Léon Charles Prudent|last4=Vandoni|first4=Carlo E.|last5=Rafelski|first5=Helga E.|publisher=CERN|others=CERN. Geneva|year=1978|series=CERN Yellow Reports: Monographs|location=Geneva|doi=10.5170/CERN-1978-012}}</ref>

Her last position was as a computer science teacher at [[Catalina Foothills High School]] in Tucson.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2007-08-05 |title=Lauren Elmegreen, Marc Rafelski (Published 2007) |work=The New York Times |language=en |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/05/fashion/weddings/05elmegreen.html |access-date=2023-08-10}}</ref>

Helga Rafelski died of cancer in November 2000 in Tucson, Arizona.
